slides.text: In 1972, an apartment tower in Tokyo was built from 140 rooms made in a factory, each meant to be swapped out for a new one.
The architect Kisho Kurokawa designed it for Ginza, in central Tokyo. Each room was a capsule about 2.5 meters wide and 4 meters long.
The capsules arrived finished and were bolted onto two concrete cores, one 11 stories tall and one 13.
Inside each: a bed, a fold-out desk, a bathroom unit, a Sony color TV and a reel-to-reel tape recorder, under one round window.
The plan was to replace the capsules every 25 years or so.
None of them was ever replaced.
Demolition began in April 2022. Before the tower came down, 23 capsules were lifted off and saved.
Today, single capsules sit in museums in San Francisco, New York, Hong Kong and Wakayama.
